item.title: Pointblank vs validate vs assertr: R Data Validation in 2026 (Which One Fits Your Pipeline?)
item.description: A column of negative revenue values can survive an entire ETL pipeline, a dashboard refresh and three weekly reports before anyone notices. In R shops the fix is almost always one of three packages: pointblank, validate or assertr — and teams routinely pick the wrong one, then fight it for a year. The mismatch is easy to explain: one is built for reporting validation results, one is built for storing validation rules as data, and one is built for stopping a pipeline the moment an assumption breaks. Those are three different jobs.

item.title: data.table vs dplyr vs tidytable in 2026: Which R Data Library Should You Actually Use?
item.description: An R script that reads a 4 GB CSV, groups by three columns and writes a summary should not take longer than your coffee break — but the same job can run in seconds or in minutes depending on which data library you load. That difference is not academic. It decides whether an analyst iterates five times an hour or twice a day, and it decides whether a laptop with 16 GB of RAM can hold the working set at all.
